title: Retail Sales: Vasudha Retail
description: Vasudha Retail is a fictional chain of 24 grocery and lifestyle stores (hypermarkets, supermarkets and express stores) across 15 Indian states and union territories. The dataset covers 2023-2024 with sampled transaction lines, month-end inventory snapshots per store and SKU, and monthly sales targets. Use it for monthly sales trends, festive seasonality, stockout impact, overstock and target attainment.

tables.name: stores
tables.description: 24 stores with city, region, format and carpet area.

columns.name: store_code
columns.description: Short store code such as VSD-001

tables.name: sales
tables.description: Sampled sales transaction lines, about one line per store per day (350 exact duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: sale_id
columns.description: Sale line identifier (duplicated for duplicate rows)

columns.name: sale_datetime
columns.description: Date and time of the sale

columns.name: sku_id
columns.description: SKU code (no product master table; see category)

columns.name: net_amount_inr
columns.description: Net line amount in INR after discount (6 rows are 100x outliers)

columns.name: payment_mode
columns.description: UPI, Card, Cash or Wallet (casing issues, ~1% NULL)

tables.name: inventory
tables.description: Month-end stock snapshot for every store and SKU, 2023-01 to 2024-12.

columns.name: stock_on_hand
columns.description: Units on hand at month end (NULL for ~1%)

columns.name: days_out_of_stock
columns.description: Days during the month the SKU was out of stock

tables.name: targets
tables.description: Monthly net sales targets per store; the East region (Kolkata, Patna, Guwahati) has no targets.

columns.name: target_net_sales_inr
columns.description: Target net sales in INR (NULL for ~3%)

columns.name: target_units
columns.description: Target units derived from the sales target

qualityIssues: sales: 350 exact duplicate rows (same sale_id twice), so sale_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint.
sales.discount_pct: NULL for ~4% of rows; net_amount_inr already reflects the discount, so it is still populated.
targets.target_net_sales_inr: ~3% NULL; no targets exist for the East region stores.
CSV only - sales.sale_datetime: ~15% of rows use DD-MM-YYYY; sales.net_amount_inr: ~25% are rupee text with Indian grouping.
CSV only - inventory.snapshot_date: ~12% of rows use DD-MM-YYYY; targets.target_net_sales_inr: ~15% are rupee text.
No product master table: sku_id and category are denormalised codes.
er:
erDiagram
  stores {
    INTEGER store_id PK
    TEXT store_code
    TEXT store_name
    TEXT city
    TEXT state
    TEXT region
    TEXT store_format

  sales {
    INTEGER sale_id PK

    TEXT sku_id
    TEXT category

    TEXT payment_mode

  inventory {
    INTEGER inventory_id PK
    TEXT snapshot_date
    INTEGER store_id FK
    TEXT sku_id
    TEXT category
    INTEGER stock_on_hand
    INTEGER reorder_level
    INTEGER units_sold_in_month
    INTEGER days_out_of_stock
  }
  targets {
    INTEGER target_id PK
    INTEGER store_id FK
    TEXT target_month
    REAL target_net_sales_inr
    INTEGER target_units
  }
  stores ||--o{ sales : "store_id"
  stores ||--o{ inventory : "store_id"
  stores ||--o{ targets : "store_id"
signals: [Instructor note] Stockouts: Velachery (Chennai), Adajan (Surat), Gomti Nagar (Lucknow) and Kharadi (Pune) stores have frequent stockouts (days_out_of_stock > 0 for many SKUs) and roughly 30% lower sales volume than peers.
[Instructor note] Diwali (Oct-Nov) and the 2024 Navratri window spike sales; Republic Day and Independence Day sale weeks give smaller spikes.
[Instructor note] Home Decor is slow-moving: about 5% of sales volume, but stock covers 6-10 months of demand, so it is overstocked.
[Instructor note] East region stores (Kolkata, Patna, Guwahati) have no targets, so target attainment can only be compared for the other regions.
[Instructor note] Targets are set at 90-115% of actual sales, so attainment clusters near 100% with a few misses.
[Instructor note] 2024 prices are about 6% higher than 2023 for every SKU, so compare volume and value separately.
[Instructor note] Sales are a sampled extract of about one transaction line per store per day, so use rates and shares rather than absolute totals.
[Instructor note] 6 net_amount outliers (100x) distort totals unless excluded.
